title: Post-training is (Massive) Supervised Learning
abstract: arXiv:2606.07527v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The prevailing paradigm for training LLMs has evolved to rely on a massive post-training phase consisting of SFT and RL. In this position paper, we argue that this methodology effectively marks a reversion to the ``pre-train then fine-tune'' approach of the BERT era, explicitly tailoring models to the desired behaviors and specific benchmarks on which they are evaluated. We begin with a historical overview of LLMs, describing the different phases of the LLM evolution. We argue that the current landscape is remarkably similar to the early days of LLMs, where task performance heavily relied on fitting the models to in-distribution datasets. To empirically demonstrate this, we compare pre-trained models to randomly initialized ones, by fine-tuning both variants on modern reasoning datasets and evaluating them on competitive math and code benchmarks. We show that models post-trained from scratch yield highly non-trivial performance

translated_title: 后训练即（大规模）监督学习
translated_abstract: 训练大语言模型（LLM）的主流范式已经演变为依赖一个由监督微调（SFT）和强化学习（RL）组成的大规模后训练阶段。在这篇立场论文中，我们认为这种方法实际上标志着向BERT时代“先预训练后微调”方法的回归，即显式地将模型定制为期望的行为以及用于评估的特定基准。我们首先对LLM进行了历史回顾，描述了LLM演化的不同阶段。我们认为当前的格局与LLM早期阶段惊人地相似，当时任务性能在很大程度上依赖于将模型拟合到分布内的数据集。为了实证证明这一点，我们将预训练模型与随机初始化的模型进行比较，在现代推理数据集上对两种变体进行微调，并在具有竞争力的数学和代码基准上进行评估。我们表明，从头开始进行后训练的模型能够取得高度可观的非平凡性能。
tldr: 这篇立场论文指出，当前由SFT和强化学习构成的大规模后训练范式本质上是向BERT时代“预训练+微调”方法的回归，并通过实验证明仅靠后训练（即使从随机初始化开始）也能在数学和代码基准上取得相当可观的成绩。
en_tdlr: This position paper argues that the current massive post-training paradigm (SFT + RL) effectively marks a reversion to the BERT-era "pre-train then fine-tune" approach, and empirically shows that models post-trained from random initialization achieve highly non-trivial performance on competitive math and code benchmarks.
